clue.text: Thereby people foil the cane

parts.note: a foil is a fencing blade, so this is a walking cane with a blade hidden inside it, by which the cane itself carries a weapon

explanation.surface: People foil an attack with a cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' reads as a verb meaning thwart, but it is the fencing sword hidden in the cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking cane concealing a blade lets its owner carry a weapon inside the stick.

clue.text: Shakedown of the finest sort

parts.note: shaking material through a sieve so the fine particles fall through and are sorted from the coarse

explanation.surface: A superior kind of police raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakedown' suggests extortion or a search; it is shaking a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing material through a sieve sorts fine particles from coarse ones by shaking.

clue.text: Kisses for all? Sound idea, mos moving

definitions.text: Kisses for all? Sound idea, mos moving

parts.words: Kisses for all? Sound idea, mos moving
parts.note: busses is an old word for kisses and the Latin omni- means for all; said together they sound like public vehicles that move most people

explanation.surface: A proposal to kiss everyone is welcomed as a fine idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busses' (kisses) for all, Latin 'omni', sounds like the name of buses that carry people about.
explanation.definitionFit: Large public road vehicles carry many passengers; the Latin name means 'for all'.

clue.text: Deemouth

parts.note: the mouth of the river Dee, and also D as a written letter; the Greek letter D names a river mouth

explanation.surface: The mouth of the river Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek letter for D shares its name with the fan of silt at a river's mouth, so the Dee's mouth is both.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular silt plain at a river mouth is named after the triangular Greek letter D.

clue.text: The birds! They're after the cat

definitions.text: The birds! They're after the cat

parts.words: The birds! They're after the cat
parts.note: small songbirds whose name follows the word for a male cat, as though the birds were chasing it

explanation.surface: Birds are chasing the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' means following in the word, TITS after TOM (a male cat), not chasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomtit is a familiar name for the blue tit or other small tit.

clue.text: May be part of Ecclesiastical Commissioners' investment policy too

definitions.text: May be part of Ecclesiastical Commissioners' investment policy too

parts.words: May be part of Ecclesiastical Commissioners' investment policy too
parts.note: church officials gain a new believer and may also change one stock into another, two senses of one verb

explanation.surface: A note on the church's financial strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church Commissioners, who manage Church of England money, might change one stock into another as well as win new believers.
explanation.definitionFit: To change stock into another form, or to bring someone over to a new faith.

clue.text: It's his turn when the tocsin starts

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the opening stretch of the alarm-bell word from right to left
only the starting letters of tocsin are used, so its final pair is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone takes a turn ringing an alarm bell.
explanation.walkthrough: The first four letters of 'tocsin' give TOCS, and 'turn' reads them backwards. 'His' points to a man from Scotland whose turn it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue presents a man whose turn it is; the answer names him by his nationality, a Scotsman.

clue.text: In a terrific hurricane hear the nightjar

indicators.note: In shows the letters sit inside the words terrific hurricane, across the word join

explanation.surface: A bird is heard calling in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'terrifiC HURRicane'.
explanation.definitionFit: The low trilling call of the nightjar, a sound you hear at dusk.

clue.text: Only sixpence out of the house in German opera

indicators.note: out of here means the coin word goes outside, wrapping round the house word

parts.note: a tanner was British slang for the old sixpence coin
Haus is German for house

explanation.surface: Only sixpence is left after leaving a house to see a German opera.
explanation.walkthrough: TANNER (old British slang for a sixpence) goes around HAUS, German for house.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's opera about the minstrel knight and the Venusberg bears that title.

clue.text: New price of a lion

annotationWithheld.why: New price of a lion (8): no parse found linking a lion to the answer's sum of money; the reference (likely topical in 1950s Britain) cannot be confirmed

clue.text: No more heat after this

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying round of a race or contest; once the deciding round comes there are none left

explanation.surface: Relief that the hot weather is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' suggests temperature, but it is a qualifying round in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The deciding round of a competition comes after all the qualifying heats.

clue.text: A model if not a paragon

definitions.text: A model if not a paragon

parts.words: A model if not a paragon
parts.note: model can mean a perfect example or a figure used to display clothes; this is the second sort

explanation.surface: Someone is a role model though not quite perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' in its sense of an ideal is ruled out; the dummy in a shop window is the other kind of model.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's dummy or a fashion model displays clothes, a model in the display sense rather than an ideal.

clue.text: A live bat fluttering in a case

indicators.note: a bat flutters about, so the letters of these three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bat is caught alive and flutters in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a box, but it is a grammatical case in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar the ablative is a noun case expressing means or separation.

clue.text: Fish in the clutch of a bird

explanation.surface: A fish is caught in a bird's claws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' suggests a set of eggs, but it is what the bird grips.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of that name; also the bar or twig a bird grips when it rests.

clue.text: Heavy horse for the big race here

definitions.text: Heavy horse for the big race here

parts.words: Heavy horse for the big race here
parts.note: a heavy draught horse breed and the famous Epsom race combine to name an English county

explanation.surface: A heavy cart horse is entered for a big race.
explanation.walkthrough: SHIRE (a heavy draught horse) after DERBY (the big flat race at Epsom) names a county of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: An English Midlands county, whose county town gave its name to a race.

clue.text: Sends Green to the Tower — or the Pit

definitions.text: Sends Green to the Tower — or the Pit

parts.words: Sends Green to the Tower — or the Pit
parts.note: green fodder is stored to ferment in a tall tower silo or in a pit dug in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone named Green is sent to the Tower of London or the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a prisoner's name sent to the Tower of London; it is green fodder put in a silo.
explanation.definitionFit: To store green fodder in a silo, a tower or pit, so it ferments into silage.

clue.text: Birds singing high, high abovethe Plain ?

definitions.text: Birds singing high, high abovethe Plain

parts.words: Birds singing high, high abovethe Plain
parts.note: a songbird that sings while climbing high, and a high mound, naming an army camp on Salisbury Plain

explanation.surface: Songbirds sing high in the sky over a plain.
explanation.walkthrough: A LARK sings as it climbs high; a HILL is high ground; together they name an army garrison on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An army garrison town on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England.

clue.text: Feature of a French vintage car ?

definitions.text: Feature of a French vintage car ?

parts.words: Feature of a French vintage car ?
parts.note: the rounded rear passenger body of an early motor car; the French word also means a wine cask, which suits vintage

explanation.surface: A collector admires a detail of an old French car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vintage' works twice: an old car, and wine, since the French word for this car body means a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded rear seating section of early cars took its name from the French for a barrel.

clue.text: Bee in elation finding a plant

indicators.note: in tells us the letter goes inside the word for elation

parts.note: euphoria is intense elation
bee is the spelt-out name of the letter B

explanation.surface: A bee is overjoyed to find a flowering plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bee' is the letter B, put inside EUPHORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurges are a large genus of plants with milky sap.

clue.text: Be altering those tartan trousers as you spread

indicators.note: altering trousers changes them, so the letters of the trouser word are rearranged

parts.note: trews are close-fitting tartan trousers worn in Scotland

explanation.surface: A tailor takes in a pair of tartan trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altering' rearranges TREWS to STREW, after BE.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter things over a surface is to strew or spread them.

clue.text: Vessel for the godly neighbour

parts.note: cleanliness is next to godliness, so the cleaning vessel is the neighbour of the godly

explanation.surface: A ship for a pious neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'cleanliness is next to godliness' makes cleaning the godly's neighbour; the vessel is a tub for laundry, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tub for laundering clothes, the cleaning vessel next to godliness in the proverb.

clue.text: High Church taper

parts.note: a tall pointed structure on a church narrows to a point; High Church also suggests a candle used in ritual

explanation.surface: A candle used in a ritualist High Church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taper' reads as a candle, but it is something tall that tapers on a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall spire rising from a church tower narrows to a point as it rises.

clue.text: South-east is sunrise for the sect

indicators.note: in a down clue rising reads the letters from bottom to top, so the words before it run backwards

explanation.surface: Sunrise in the south-east matters to a religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reverses IS SUN to NUSSI after SE; the sect is a Muslim order of Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim brotherhood founded in North Africa that became dominant in Libya.

clue.text: To cane makes smart

explanation.surface: Beating someone makes them sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as a verb meaning sting, but it is the adjective meaning stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat with a whippy stick makes that sound; and as an adjective it means fashionable or posh.

clue.text: Children of Exodus

explanation.surface: The children of Israel in the Book of Exodus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exodus' looks like the Bible book; it is a going out, an outflow.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are one's descendants; and an outflow or emergence is a going forth.

clue.text: Open it for air

parts.note: air means a tune, so this is a volume you open to find tunes to sing

explanation.surface: Advice to open a window to let in fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' suggests ventilation; it is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of tunes and lyrics is opened to find a melody to sing.

clue.text: Sounds of disapproval of drink

indicators.note: sounds of tells us the word for jeers is heard and gives a spelling like it

parts.note: boos are cries of disapproval

explanation.surface: Disapproving noises about drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOS said out loud gives the word for alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Cutter outward bound

explanation.surface: A cutter, a small ship, sets sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' and 'outward bound' suggest a ship setting off; they are a blade and an outer boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharp side of a blade cuts; and the outer limit or rim of something bounds it.

clue.text: Debars from conducting

parts.note: conducting here is passing on heat or electricity, not leading an orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader is banned from the podium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conducting' suggests leading a band; it is passing electricity or heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping a wire or wall in non-conducting material stops heat or current passing through it.

clue.text: " That maiden, with white fire laden " (Shelley)

definitions.text: " That maiden, with white fire laden " (Shelley)

parts.words: " That maiden, with white fire laden " (Shelley)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Shelley's poem The Cloud, where the round moon is the maiden

explanation.surface: A line of Shelley with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Shelley's 'The Cloud', describing the moon; the missing word means round like a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The full moon, round as a globe, is described as sphere-shaped in Shelley's line.

clue.text: A currency's reduced costs

parts.note: costs here are expenses, and a colloquial shortened form of that word is current in speech

explanation.surface: A currency is devalued, so prices fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currency' suggests money; it means a word in current use, here the clipped form of 'expenses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for expenses: the costs a worker claims back.

clue.text: The old boy can read and write-and blot!

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
someone who can read and write is literate

explanation.surface: A former pupil who is literate still blots his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blot' as a verb means to wipe out, as in 'blot out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To blot out writing is to efface or wipe it away entirely.
